alumni.name: Stan Green
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

Stan Green was an end and co-captain with Jimmy Duffy on Saugus’ 1939 North Shore championship team, which finished 9–1–1. After becoming a starting end the previous fall, he developed into a receiver and defender whom coach Buzz Harvey rated among his best players. The 1939 yearbook credits Green with a touchdown in the 21–0 victory over Amesbury and describes his pass-catching partnership with John “Iron Mike” Harrington as an important part of the 13–7 win over Wakefield. It also singles him out among the linemen who disrupted Wakefield’s running game. Green also scored in the 38–6 Thanksgiving win over Danvers.

His senior honors included Boston Herald and Boston Post All-Scholastic recognition, and he continued his football career at Columbia. The captain-election clipping records ten votes each for Green and Duffy and explains that they would lead alternate games, preserving the unusual arrangement behind his championship-season leadership.

alumni.name: John “Iron Mike” Harrington
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

John “Iron Mike” Harrington was a leading halfback and two-time co-captain during one of Saugus High’s strongest early eras. He contributed to the 1939 North Shore championship team and held the ball for Joseph Bucchiere’s decisive field goal in the 3–0 victory over Salem. The yearbooks identify him as a co-captain for both the 1940 and 1941 seasons. He scored two touchdowns in the 38–6 Thanksgiving win over Danvers in 1939.

As a senior in 1941, Harrington helped Henry Toczylowski’s Sachems finish 10–0–1 and win the Class C state championship. The season review pairs him with Ed Shipulski as the team’s “touchdown twins.” Harrington scored the tying touchdown in the closing minute against Leominster, broke scoring runs of 37 yards against Gloucester and 47 yards against Swampscott, and threw the late touchdown pass to Claude Collette that secured a 6–0 victory over Marblehead. In the 12–6 Thanksgiving finale over Wakefield, the Boston Globe credited Harrington with carrying much of the offensive load on the drives that set up Welcome Goss’s two touchdowns. His recognition included the Boston Globe’s 1941 All-Scholastic second team at back and its North Shore All-Scholastic eleven.

His 1942 senior biography records four years of football alongside participation in baseball, basketball, hockey and track. A later Saugus Advocate retrospective reports that a serious automobile accident after graduation curtailed his playing career and that he subsequently returned to Saugus as an assistant football coach.

alumni.name: Art Statuto
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1989.

Art Statuto’s career connected Saugus High’s championship years with Notre Dame and professional football. A member of the 1941 Class C state champions, he played center and contributed on defense as well as offense. The 1942 yearbook singled out his work against both the pass and the run in Saugus’ 26–0 victory over Revere. The Boston Globe recognized him with All-Scholastic honorable mention at center in both 1941 and 1942. Notre Dame’s contemporary player biography credits him with four football letters and two baseball letters at Saugus. His 1943 senior biography also records service as junior class president.

Statuto joined Notre Dame’s 1943 squad and later returned to the Irish after wartime Navy service. Notre Dame’s 1946 Football Review describes 37 months in the Navy, service as an engineering officer aboard a landing ship, and football with the Fort Pierce Navy team. His Irish squad membership spans the national championship seasons of 1943, 1946 and 1947; his role was as a reserve center. A university retrospective identifies him as a reserve center whose subsequent professional success reflected the remarkable depth of those teams. The Saugus Advocate also records his selection to the 1948 College Football All-Star Team.

He went on to play center for the Buffalo Bills of the All-America Football Conference in 1948 and 1949 and the Los Angeles Rams of the NFL in 1950. His Rams career is also preserved in the promotional football card in this archive.

alumni.name: Doug Waybright
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1988.

Doug Waybright was a member of Saugus’ 1941 Class C state championship squad and developed into a versatile back and team leader. In his senior season of 1943, he shared the captaincy with Jim MacDougall and earned selection to the Essex County All-Star squad for its meeting with Greater Boston at Manning Bowl.

The yearbook’s 1943 season account highlights his impact on both sides of the ball. In the 32–7 victory over Newburyport, Waybright scored two early touchdowns and added a 67-yard interception return for another score. Other accounts credit him with an interception against Marblehead and a long punt return against Wakefield that was called back, illustrating the range of ways he could change a game.

At Notre Dame, Waybright moved to end and became a late-season starter in 1944. In the 28–7 win over Great Lakes that December, he recovered a fumble in the end zone to break a 7–7 tie. Notre Dame’s 1944 Football Review also credits him with six Saugus letters—two apiece in football, track and basketball. Following wartime service, he was a member of the Irish’s 1947 and 1949 national championship teams. The university’s 1948 Football Review reports that he resumed his Irish career in 1947 after two years in the infantry and had earned two Notre Dame monograms by the end of 1948. Notre Dame’s draft history also lists his selection by Buffalo in the 1948 AAFC draft, before his final national championship season with the Irish in 1949.

His Saugus legacy extended to youth sports and community service. A later hometown retrospective recalls his work with young athletes and the naming of the Waybright elementary school in his memory after his death at age 38.

alumni.name: Art Spinney
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

Art Spinney captained Saugus’ unbeaten 1944 Class B state championship team and earned Boston Globe All-Scholastic first-team recognition at end. The Sachems went 10–0 in the regular season, posted eight shutouts and clinched the class title with a 26–0 Thanksgiving win at Wakefield. He had received Globe honorable mention the previous season and was selected for the 1944 North Shore All-Stars. His size, blocking and play on both sides of the line helped make him one of the outstanding Sachems of that era.

At Boston College (Class of 1950), Spinney was a four-year starting end and captain of the 1949 Eagles. BC’s Hall of Fame biography credits him with two All-New England selections for his blocking and receiving. His 24 catches in 1948 set a school single-season record at the time. His college achievements earned induction into the Boston College Varsity Club Athletic Hall of Fame in 1972.

He played professionally for the Baltimore Colts in 1950 and from 1953 through 1960, developing into a standout offensive guard after beginning at end. He entered the U.S. Army after playing two league games in 1950, with former Saugus teammate Thomas Sheehan among the same group of draftees. Baltimore’s 1960 team guide praised his pulling and his range of blocking skills after his return from a 1957 leg injury. He earned All-Pro recognition and Pro Bowl selections for the 1959 and 1960 seasons and helped the Colts win consecutive NFL championships in 1958 and 1959. He later coached the Boston Patriots’ offensive line from 1962 through 1968. His son Steve also became a Saugus football captain and All-Star.

alumni.name: George Laskey
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

George Laskey was a powerful runner whose football honors span both the 1946 and 1947 seasons. The preserved 1946 North Shore All-Star roster lists him at halfback. His 1946 honors also included Boston Globe All-Scholastic honorable mention at back. As a senior in 1947, he earned the Lynn Item’s All-Scholastic selection at fullback, recognition on the Boston Post’s All-Scholastic team and selection to the Globe’s Class B All-Star backfield.

Laskey’s running figures prominently in the yearbooks’ game accounts. In 1946 he scored the touchdown and ran in the extra point in Saugus’ first win over Peabody, a 7–0 upset at Manning Bowl. He opened the winning 52-yard drive with a 20-yard run and finished it by diving over two defenders. He also helped produce wins over Swampscott and Marblehead. His running and all-around play stood out in John Janusas’s spring scrimmage against Lowell. Under Janusas that fall, he remained a central part of the attack alongside quarterback Earle Dudman and fellow backs Ernie Anganis and Frank Forti. On October 4, he helped erase a 13–0 deficit against Chelsea: his long kickoff return launched the rally, and his nine-yard touchdown run put Saugus ahead in the 21–13 win. A week later, he rushed for 102 yards on 13 carries and scored both touchdowns in a 14–6 victory over Amesbury—one on a pass from Sal Nicolo that covered 60 yards in all and the other on an eight-yard run. He caught a 20-yard scoring pass in the 14–0 win over Lynn English, then ran for touchdowns of three and 15 yards in the 20–0 win over Swampscott. The surviving reports account for six touchdowns for Saugus that fall, four rushing and two receiving, and an interception with a 12-yard return against Brookline. His North Shore All-Star touchdown was separate.

Lynn Classical standout George Bullard, a teammate of Harry Agganis, called Laskey the best individual player he faced. Laskey and Agganis shared the North Shore backfield in back-to-back all-star wins over the Suburban stars at Manning Bowl, 14–7 in 1946 and 19–6 in 1947.

He was selected for the Massachusetts All-Star team for the November 29, 1947 game in Dover, though he did not play. His recognition continued beyond the school schedule. A Boston Post photograph dated December 8, 1947 shows Laskey scoring on a two-yard plunge for the North Shore All-Stars at Manning Bowl in the 19–6 victory over Suburban Boston. A later awards report identifies him as the 1947 recipient of the Thomas R. Atkins Memorial Trophy. His 1948 senior biography records four years of football participation, preserving the school career behind those regional honors.

alumni.name: Dan Murphy
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1994.

Dan “Danny” Murphy was a guard and co-captain, alongside Salvatore “Sardi” Nicolo, on John Janusas’ 1949 North Shore co-championship and Exchange Bowl championship team. The Sachems finished 10–1, closing the season with their dramatic 7–6 victory over Weymouth. Murphy’s role at the line of scrimmage helped provide the foundation for a backfield featuring the Nicolo brothers and Fred Quinlan.

His senior season brought widespread recognition. His honors included a Boston Globe All-Scholastic reserve selection in 1949, along with Lynn Item and Boston Sunday Post selections at guard. The Post’s November 27, 1949 page includes his portrait among its All-Scholastic players. A separate school awards report identifies Murphy as the team’s outstanding lineman and the recipient of the Thomas R. Atkins Memorial Trophy.

Murphy’s leadership extended beyond football. His 1950 senior biography identifies him as senior class president, a four-year football participant and senior co-captain, with additional participation in baseball, hockey and track. The 1949 “A family affair” clipping also pairs him with his younger brother Charlie among the six sets of brothers on the Sachems’ squad. Together, the yearbook and newspaper pages preserve a player who represented Saugus as a lineman, captain and student leader.

alumni.name: Salvatore 'Sardi' Nicolo
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

A three-year Sachems running back and co-captain with Dan Murphy in 1949, Salvatore “Sardi” Nicolo combined speed, power and elusive running to become Saugus’ leading ground gainer and the North Shore’s scoring champion. Harvey L. Southward’s regular-season wrap-up credits him with 16 touchdowns and three extra points for 99 points, ahead of Beverly’s Bill Ransom with 84. Sardi finished that race with two touchdowns and a rushing extra point against Peabody on Thanksgiving. His 1949 honors included Lynn Item, Boston Globe and Boston Sunday Post All-Scholastic selections, R.A.A. All-Scholastic recognition, and high-school All-America honorable mention from the Wigwam Wisemen of America.

As a sophomore in 1947, Nicolo backed up captain Ernie Anganis at left halfback, threw a touchdown pass to George Laskey against Amesbury and set up a touchdown with a long completion against Marblehead. After the 1948 season, the Saugus Lions Club honored him and captain Ed Falasca as the team’s outstanding players. His teammates elected him and Dan Murphy co-captains for 1949. A three-touchdown game against Chelsea moved him into the North Shore scoring lead with nine touchdowns and 54 points through five games in 1949. In the 25–7 victory over Marblehead on November 12, 1949, he broke a 69-yard touchdown run on a triple reverse. Saugus ultimately shared the North Shore championship with Gloucester and finished 10–1. In the Exchange Bowl against Weymouth, Sardi caught the decisive 50-yard, over-the-shoulder touchdown pass from his brother Richie; Leo Kane’s extra point completed the 7–6 championship victory. The postgame column reported that Sardi played most of the game with a double dislocation of his thumb. Including the bowl, Sardi scored 17 touchdowns and 105 points. The previous fall, Sardi had scored on runs of 14 and 12 yards in a 14–0 upset of Swampscott.

A Louisiana newspaper reported that Nicolo spent a short time at Wake Forest before joining LSU, where he earned varsity letters from 1952 through 1954. At LSU, Sardi produced a play that remained in the school record book for decades: a 94-yard touchdown run against Rice on October 4, 1952. LSU’s contemporary record guides and later game notes credit it as a share of the school’s longest rushing play and offensive play from scrimmage. That mark stood until Derrius Guice’s 96-yard touchdown against Arkansas on November 12, 2016—more than 64 years later.

Sardi’s son John (Saugus Class of 1976) followed him as an All-Scholastic running back, then won football and baseball national championships at Ithaca College. Sardi’s son Peter “Pete” Nicolo also played for the Sachems as a wide receiver from 1976 to 1979. John’s sons Sal and Mike continued the family tradition: Sal started at fullback and linebacker in 2001 and 2002, while Mike earned multiple All-Scholastic honors and set a then-school single-game rushing record. Sardi, John and Mike also represent three generations of Saugus High Athletic Hall of Fame inductees.

alumni.name: Richard “Richie” Nicolo
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1988.

Richard “Richie” Nicolo directed John Janusas’ T offense as a passer, runner and punter and helped Saugus win consecutive Exchange Bowl championships in 1949 and 1950. His 1950 Lynn Item All-Scholastic profile praised his ball handling and his ability to punish defenses either through the air or by running when defenders dropped into coverage. He also received Boston Globe All-Scholastic honorable mention at quarterback in 1950.

In the 1949 Exchange Bowl, his 50-yard touchdown pass to his brother Sardi tied Weymouth in the closing seconds; Leo Kane’s extra point completed the 7–6 victory. The following year, Richie accounted for all four Saugus touchdowns in the 30–12 Exchange Bowl win over Brockton, scoring on a five-yard run and a 60-yard interception return and passing for two. The game officials selected him for the Most Valuable Player trophy, presented at the postgame banquet. The victory completed an 8–2 season.

Nicolo was also selected for the North Shore squad in the December 3, 1950 All-Star game against Suburban Boston, but a knee injury kept him on the bench. Boston College’s official lettermen directory confirms his 1951 football letter. A contemporary Globe practice report explains that BC tried the Saugus quarterback at halfback to take advantage of his sprinting ability while retaining the possibility of passes from that position.

alumni.name: Christie Serino
alumni.bio:
Christie “Chris” Serino, Saugus High Class of 1967, starred at quarterback for the Sachems. A Lynn Item and Northeastern Conference football All-Star in 1966, the quarterback helped Saugus finish 7–2. His junior-year Thanksgiving performance included 12 completions in 16 attempts for 103 yards in a 35–12 victory over Peabody in 1965. He earned the Sachems’ MVP award in football, baseball and hockey in 1967.

His senior season included several decisive quarterback performances. In a 36–8 win over Beverly, his passes repeatedly put Jim Paolini in scoring position. Against Lynn English, Serino scored on a five-yard run and a lateral from Paolini in a 40–0 victory. He then accounted for three touchdowns in the 35–14 win over Winthrop: runs of 22 and 20 yards and a 25-yard touchdown pass to Chuck Bilton. Selected for the 1967 Harry Agganis All-Star game, he was unable to participate after an appendectomy the previous week.

Serino continued all three sports at American International College, graduating in 1971. A quarterback and defensive back in football and a wing in hockey, he earned All-ECAC honors in both sports. In baseball, he received Topps All-America recognition after batting .472 in 1971 to lead the College Division and set AIC’s single-season record. He also received AIC’s 1971 President’s Cup as its outstanding senior athlete. His baseball success followed three Boston Globe All-Scholastic honorable mentions at shortstop for Saugus, in 1965, 1966 and 1967.

His coaching career spanned high school, prep school and college athletics. As Saugus’s head hockey coach from 1980–1987, he compiled a 100–23–14 record, won three Northeastern Conference championships and earned Eastern Massachusetts and NEC Coach of the Year honors in 1986–87. He subsequently guided Northfield Mount Hermon hockey to a 47–21–3 record over three seasons.

At the University of New Hampshire, Serino served as an assistant hockey coach from 1991–1998 and head baseball coach from 1994–1996. His 1995 baseball team won a school-record 26 games. In hockey, he helped UNH reach five NCAA tournaments, share the 1996–97 Hockey East regular-season championship and advance to the 1998 Frozen Four. He then became Merrimack’s head hockey coach in 1998, leading the Warriors through 2005 and also serving as athletic director.

At Malden Catholic, Serino became head hockey coach and athletic director in 2005, building the Lancers into a leading program. His teams went 95–29–19 and reached five Super 8 tournaments in six seasons, capped by the 2011 Super 8 championship. The program repeated as champion in 2012 while he was on leave from coaching.

Serino was inducted into the Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame in its inaugural class in 1987, the Massachusetts High School Hockey Hall of Fame in 2001 and AIC’s Athletic Hall of Fame in 2006. Saugus later named its high-school stadium in his honor. His son Matt Serino is Saugus High School’s athletic director; his appointment was announced in June 2024, with his tenure beginning July 1, 2024.

alumni.name: Doug Mackie
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

Doug Mackie was a two-time Boston Globe, Boston Herald and Lynn Item All-Scholastic in 1974 and 1975 and a Parade and Blue Chip Magazine high-school All-American in 1975. A captain of Saugus’ 9–1 Northeastern Conference co-championship team in 1975, he was also selected for the 1976 Agganis All-Star game. The Globe’s January 12, 1976 recruiting feature identifies him as its Player of the Year and describes his meetings with Ohio State coach Woody Hayes.

Mackie went on to Ohio State, where injuries interrupted his college career. A later Item feature recounts four knee operations before he earned a starting offensive-tackle role with Steve Spurrier’s Tampa Bay Bandits in 1983. He started Tampa Bay’s 21–17 season-opening win over Boston and earned early recognition among the new USFL’s offensive linemen.

He played for the New Jersey Generals in 1984 and 1985, earning College & Pro Football Newsweekly second-team All-Pro recognition in 1984. His blocking helped Herschel Walker set the USFL single-season rushing record with 2,411 yards in 1985. His NFL opportunities included the New York Giants in 1982 and New Orleans Saints in 1986; he played three regular-season games for the Atlanta Falcons in 1987.

The Item ranked Mackie No. 19 in its 1999 “Century’s Top 100 Players” series across multiple sports, recognizing a career that connected Saugus’ championship resurgence with Ohio State and professional football.

alumni.name: Steve Gannon
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1988.

Steve Gannon’s varsity emergence included three sacks of Danvers quarterback Bobby Sheridan as a sophomore in 1973. He later shared the captaincy of the 1975 Sachems, who finished 9–1 and shared the Northeastern Conference title, and was selected for the 1976 Agganis All-Star game.

His Saugus contributions included both defense and fullback play. His 1975 Item All-Star capsule credits him with 512 rushing yards, blocking for John Nicolo and four team defensive-player-of-the-week honors in eight games. He scored on an 85-yard run at Lynn English and was selected as a defensive interior lineman on the 1975 NEC All-Star team.

At Holy Cross, Gannon developed into a leading defensive lineman. He earned first-team All-ECAC honors and the Davitt Award as the team’s top defensive lineman as a senior in 1979, when he led the Crusaders with 143 tackles—the most in recorded school history at the time. During his junior year in 1978, he helped lead the Crusaders to an overall record of 7-4, including victories over Air Force, Army and Boston College. Holy Cross inducted him into its Athletic Hall of Fame in 2020. After college he had two NFL tryouts, one with the New York Giants and one with the Cincinnati Bengals both in 1980. After his playing days ended he got involved in coaching youth and high school football, being an assistant coach on John Nicolo's Sachems teams (2001-2004).

The Gannon family’s Sachems football tradition continued with Steve’s sons, Rob Gannon and John Gannon. Rob started at wide receiver and defensive back in 2002, then at quarterback and defensive back in 2003 and 2004. John played on the Saugus offensive and defensive lines during the 2001 and 2002 seasons.

alumni.name: John Nicolo
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

A two-time Lynn Item All-Scholastic (1974 and 1975), Northeastern Conference All-Star and 1975 Boston Herald All-Scholastic, John Nicolo helped lead Saugus to a 9–1 record and a share of the 1975 NEC championship as a senior captain. As a sophomore in 1973, he came off the bench to help set up both touchdowns in a 14–7 win over Danvers and ran for 90 yards against Malden Catholic. His junior-year Item profile records 1,110 rushing yards, nine touchdowns (eight rushing and one on a 66-yard punt return against Lynn Classical), three interceptions and 378 combined punt- and kickoff-return yards in 1974. His senior season included the state Division II scoring championship with 109 points and four touchdown passes. His contemporary Item All-Scholastic profile lists 1,205 rushing yards at 5.5 yards per carry. A 1998 Item retrospective credits him with 1,500 yards. He received the 1975 Thom McAn North Shore Player of the Year award after the Item sports staff selected him as its outstanding football player. A 1976 Agganis All-Star Game preview listed him on the North squad and credited him with 2,550 rushing yards on 415 carries over his Saugus career.

Nicolo delivered as a runner, passer, defender and kicker. In October 1974, he rushed for 111 yards on 15 carries and scored in a victory over Lynn English. In the 1975 opener against Winthrop, he ran for 117 yards and a touchdown, threw two touchdown passes, returned a punt 27 yards and intercepted a pass. He later rushed for 175 yards and two touchdowns at Beverly. In the 1975 comeback at Salem, he gained 134 yards on 29 carries and repeatedly converted third downs during the final 80-yard drive. After Jay LeBranti’s 25-yard touchdown pass to Frank Scuzzarella with 47 seconds remaining, Nicolo kicked the winning extra point for a 15–14 victory. On Thanksgiving, he returned a blocked field goal 80 yards for the only touchdown in a 6–0 win over Peabody. His Item All-Scholastic capsule records coach Mike Ginolfi’s assessment of his exceptional two-way play. The Item later ranked him No. 20 in its 1999 “Century’s Top 100 Players” series across multiple sports.

On the baseball diamond at Saugus, Nicolo was a two-time Northeastern Conference All-Star. He earned 1974 Boston Globe All-Scholastic honorable mention at second base and was named a 1975 NEC All-Star infielder. The Saugus Boosters named him the 1976 boys’ Chief Drew Award recipient, and baseball coach Lenny Wall named him the team’s top player.

At Ithaca College, Nicolo earned four letters in both football and baseball and started at running back for his final three seasons. The Item credited him with 272 rushing yards and two touchdowns as a freshman on Ithaca’s junior varsity. He earned All-East and All-Conference football honors in 1978 and 1979 and Associated Press second-team Division III All-American recognition in 1979, when the Bombers defeated Wittenberg 14–10 in the Stagg Bowl to win the NCAA Division III national championship. Ithaca’s full-season 1979 statistics credit him with 880 rushing yards, nine rushing touchdowns and 1,109 all-purpose yards, including 133 yards on punt returns. A contemporary championship recap credits him with 37 rushing yards on 15 carries in the Stagg Bowl, including a run that helped set up Ithaca’s opening score. His individual Hall of Fame biography credits his college career with 1,817 rushing yards and 20 touchdowns, both fifth in program history at the time of that account.

As senior captain and shortstop, he then helped Ithaca win the 1980 NCAA Division III baseball national championship. He went 5-for-6 with three RBI in the 12–5 title-game victory over Marietta and was named College World Series Most Valuable Player after setting tournament records with 12 hits and nine runs. He earned All-World Series recognition in 1978 and 1980, All-East baseball honors in 1979 and 1980, and Independent College Athletic Conference baseball Player of the Year honors in both seasons. Ithaca named him its 1980 Ben Light Award recipient as Male Athlete of the Year. A contemporary 1980 newspaper report also described him as a two-sport Division III All-American.

That summer, Auburn of the New York–Penn League called him back after an earlier tryout. The supplied “Saugus’ Nicolo gets a pro shot” clipping reports that he played second base against Elmira and went 2-for-4 in his debut. He played for the Auburn Americans in 1980, batting .260 in the New York–Penn League. His Ithaca Hall of Fame recognition includes his individual induction in 1986 and inductions with the 1979 football champions in 2014 and the 1980 baseball champions in 2019.

He later helped rebuild the Saugus Pop Warner program, served as Saugus Sachems head football coach from 2001 to 2004, and was interim Saugus High School Athletic Director from 2003 to 2004.

Salvatore “Sardi” Nicolo, his son John and his grandson Mike represent three generations of Sachems football and Saugus High Athletic Hall of Fame inductees. John’s brother Peter “Pete” Nicolo played wide receiver for the Sachems from 1976 to 1979. John’s sons Sal and Mike both played for Saugus. Sal was a two-way starter at fullback and linebacker in 2001 and 2002.

alumni.name: Steve Peach
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1991.

Steve Peach was Saugus’ versatile quarterback, safety and kicking specialist and the first player to earn three Item football All-Star selections, in 1978, 1979 and 1980. Later Item team announcements identify him as the original three-time selection. His 1981 senior biography also records captaincies in football and baseball and three years of basketball.

The newspaper capsules trace his development. As a sophomore in 1978, he passed for 1,050 yards and 11 touchdowns, ran for three scores and intercepted four passes. In 1979 he completed 108 of 206 passes for 1,489 yards and 14 touchdowns, added four rushing touchdowns, kicked a 48-yard field goal and averaged 39 yards per punt. On defense, he led the Sachems with six interceptions and three fumble recoveries. His 1980 senior capsule credits him with 1,200 passing yards, eight touchdown passes and eight touchdowns scored, plus a 38-yard punting average.

His best games displayed that versatility. In the 46–14 win over Lynn English in 1978, he completed all five passes for 241 yards and four touchdowns and kicked four extra points. In the 25–24 upset of previously unbeaten Lynn Classical in 1979, Peach completed 14 of 27 passes for 245 yards and two touchdowns, ran for two scores and kicked the extra point that supplied the winning margin. With 11 seconds remaining, he then broke up Classical’s two-point conversion pass to preserve the victory. On Thanksgiving in 1980, he completed five of nine passes for 100 yards and two touchdowns and returned an interception 40 yards for a score as Saugus defeated Peabody, 40–6.

Peach was selected for the North squad in the 1981 Shriners Football Classic, whose Boston Globe preview noted his Syracuse scholarship. He subsequently played at Syracuse before transferring to Boston College. BC’s official record book lists him at quarterback/punter in 1984 and 1985, and a hometown retrospective recalls his role as Doug Flutie’s backup and the Eagles’ Cotton Bowl punter. His career stands out for its combination of passing, defense, kicking and participation in three high-school sports.

Further Globe reporting of the 1978 Lynn English game identifies Peach’s four first-quarter touchdown passes as covering 55, 83, 42 and nine yards. He completed all five attempts for 241 yards and kicked four extra points as Saugus scored 40 points in the opening quarter. On Thanksgiving against Peabody, Peach threw his 11th touchdown pass of the season to John Rouleau, kicked a 30-yard field goal and converted three extra points in the 30–14 victory.

alumni.name: Darren McCullough
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1997.

Darren McCullough ranks among the best all-around players in Sachems history and is one of the few Saugus players to earn Lynn Item All-Scholastic honors twice.

As a junior in 1985, he recorded 123 tackles and four interceptions while playing linebacker and defensive back. On offense, he rushed for 442 yards and added 232 receiving yards, finishing with six total touchdowns. He earned Northeastern Conference All-Star honors that season, and the Boston Globe listed him on the East roster for the 1986 Harry Agganis All-Star game.

As a senior in 1986, McCullough again led the team in tackles and rushed for 1,081 yards and 11 touchdowns. His standout performance came against Danvers, when he rushed for 225 yards and four touchdowns while also making 16 tackles. That effort earned him the Item/Coca-Cola Gold Helmet Award.

His senior honors also included Northeastern Conference All-Star recognition at back and selection to the North squad for the 1987 Shriners Football Classic. He continued in college football at Springfield, whose 1987 roster lists him as a running back from Saugus.

alumni.name: Marc Fauci
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2000.

Marc Fauci was a two-time Lynn Item All-Scholastic and a Boston Globe All-Scholastic as a senior, when he also won the NEC football Most Valuable Player award.

As a sophomore in 1987, Fauci threw 12 touchdown passes, ran for four scores and earned Northeastern Conference All-Star honors at defensive back. The Sachems went 7–3 and beat Peabody 21–20 on Thanksgiving.

His senior Item capsule provides a detailed measure of that impact: 440 career tackles and 19 interceptions, with the team tackle lead in three consecutive seasons. In 1989 he averaged 14 tackles per game, recovered four fumbles and contributed 757 rushing yards and 743 passing yards on offense. The capsule also credits him with four career Gold Helmet awards, honor-roll standing and three terms as class president.

Fauci was also chosen for the 1990 Shriners Football Classic and the 1990 Agganis All-Star game. In the Agganis game, he earned East MVP honors as the East rallied for a 21–20 victory.

At Boston University he began at strong safety, becoming a freshman starter and earning Yankee Conference Rookie of the Week after an 11-tackle, one-interception, two-pass-breakup performance against Rhode Island. He led the team in tackles as a junior with 90 and was selected as a team tri-captain, then moved to middle linebacker for his senior season. He served as a college captain in both his junior and senior seasons. He helped lead the Terriers to a 12–1 finish in 1993, including an 11–0 regular season—the program’s first unbeaten and untied regular season. A first-team All-Yankee Conference and second-team All-ECAC selection in 1993, as well as a second-team All-America selection by The Sports Network and National Weekly Football Gazette and a third-team All-America selection by the Associated Press, Fauci played linebacker and was credited by his Hall of Fame biography with top-five career totals in primary, assisted and total tackles. He entered the Boston University Athletic Hall of Fame in 2010.

alumni.name: Dan Schena
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2001.

Dan Schena was a senior tri-captain and standout on both lines for Saugus’ 8–2 team in 1990. Alongside fellow captains Ryan Magnasco and Chris Mikulski, he helped lead the final Sachems team coached by Kevin Ward. Saugus outscored opponents 284–128 and placed seven seniors on the Northeastern Conference All-Star team. Schena scored on an end-zone fumble recovery in the 20–0 win over Salem and earned Division 3 All-Star honors on the defensive line.

Schena’s own 1990 Lynn Item All-Star capsule describes a 6-foot-3, 240-pound lineman with unusual speed: he was the team’s third-fastest player. He made more than 100 tackles, earned NEC All-Star recognition and anchored a defense whose strength began up front. Ward’s assessment placed him among the program’s outstanding linemen since Doug Mackie.

The yearbook remembers the team’s closeness with its coaches as well as its victories, placing Schena within a senior class celebrated for both achievement and shared memories. He continued his football career at Northeastern University, whose official all-time lettermen list records varsity letters in each season from 1992 through 1995. Those four college seasons extend a football career that began with distinction on both sides of the line at Saugus.

alumni.name: Mike Mabee
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2006.

Mike Mabee was a senior co-captain, quarterback and defensive contributor at the center of Saugus’ 1995 revival. A multisport athlete and Lynn Item football All-Star, he helped the Sachems end a 34-game losing streak and finish 6–4, their first winning season since 1990.

His 1995 Item capsule records an efficient passing season: 61 completions in 95 attempts for 720 yards and six touchdowns. He also carried 60 times for 360 yards and seven touchdowns. His impact extended to defense, where he was the team’s second-leading tackler and recorded six interceptions and two fumble recoveries. A leg injury limited him during part of the season; the capsule emphasizes the difference his availability made to the offense.

Mabee helped deliver two defining victories. In the 25–0 win over Winthrop that ended the losing streak, he threw for a touchdown as Saugus combined a productive offense with two critical defensive stands near its goal line. Later, in the 50–20 win over Lynn English at Manning Bowl that secured a winning season, he threw two touchdown passes, ran for a score and intercepted two passes. Those performances capture the breadth of his contribution: he could direct the offense, gain yards himself and help take the ball away on defense.

Mabee’s talent also carried onto the baseball diamond. The Item’s 1996 Agganis preview identified him as Saugus’ ace pitcher and as an All-Star selection in both football and baseball. He continued in football at Plymouth State: the official rosters list him as a defensive back in 1996 and a quarterback in 1997.

Mabee returned to the Saugus sideline as interim head coach in 2018 and led the Sachems to a 4–7 finish.

alumni.name: LJ McKanas
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2007.

A senior captain and Boston Globe, Boston Herald and Lynn Item All-Scholastic, L.J. McKanas helped turn Saugus into a competitive program in the mid-1990s. His 1996 Item capsule names him NEC Offensive Player of the Year and credits him with 1,365 rushing yards, 424 receiving yards, two kickoff-return touchdowns and two Gold Helmet awards. The Globe credits him with more than 2,500 all-purpose yards and 20 total touchdowns. In the 41–34 win at Danvers, he caught a 44-yard touchdown from Ryan Leahy and ran for three more. On Thanksgiving at Peabody, he caught a 74-yard touchdown pass, ran for a 15-yard score and returned a kickoff 74 yards for a touchdown. He established school rushing and touchdown marks during his Saugus career. In the 1995 breakthrough against Winthrop, he rushed for 178 yards and two touchdowns in the 25–0 win that ended Saugus’ 34-game losing streak. He was selected for both the 1997 Shriners and Agganis games. His two-point run put the North ahead 14–10 in its 29–17 Shriners victory. In the Agganis game he gained 52 yards on 11 carries as the East won 26–0.

McKanas earned 11 Saugus letters in football, track and baseball, captaining all three as a senior. At Northeastern, he redshirted in 1997, then set a rookie rushing mark with 832 yards. Despite injuries, he set a then-school record with 225 rushing yards on 47 carries in a 35–27 upset of Connecticut and ran for 172 yards and three touchdowns against James Madison. Other standout games included 223 rushing yards and three touchdowns against Saint Mary’s. As a senior he established school season marks of 342 carries, 1,756 rushing yards and 14 rushing touchdowns, with nine 100-yard games. Highlights included 242 yards against Massachusetts and 161 yards with two touchdowns in a 20–7 upset of Delaware. He averaged 159.6 rushing yards per game in 2001, second nationally in Division I and first in the Atlantic 10, and finished with 3,692 career rushing yards, then a Northeastern record. His honors included team MVP, All-New England, All-Conference, first-team Hanson All-America and the Harry Agganis/Harold Zimman Award as New England’s outstanding senior collegiate football player. Northeastern inducted him into its Hall of Fame in 2009.

A Boston Sunday Globe article dated April 28, 2002 chronicled his pursuit of an NFL opportunity as an undrafted free agent; an NFL roster affiliation is not established by that article. In 2014, McKanas competed on CBS’s Survivor: Cagayan and finished ninth.

alumni.name: Anthony “Beave” Barbanti
alumni.bio:
A two-time Lynn Item All-Scholastic, Anthony “Beave” Barbanti was a three-year starter on both the offensive and defensive lines and a cornerstone of the Sachems during his junior and senior seasons.

His senior season in 2003 was his finest: he recorded 75 tackles, including 11 tackles for loss, and three sacks. He was equally dominant on the offensive line, helping clear the way for Mike Nicolo’s record-setting rushing performances. Barbanti’s strength, consistency and two-way play made him a key part of Saugus’ success.

The 2003 Item capsule identifies Barbanti as a senior co-captain and a three-time Northeastern Conference All-Star, in addition to his two Item selections. His 2002 junior capsule had already described him as a two-year starter whom the coaches regarded as their best player throughout that season. As a junior he recovered a fumble against Gloucester and recorded a 10-yard sack at Peabody on Thanksgiving.

Barbanti was selected for the North squad in the 2004 Shriners Football Classic. The contributed season-history workbook also records his selection for the 2004 Agganis All-Star game.

A 2003 Thanksgiving preview singled out Barbanti's blocking alongside Mark Spadafora and identified him as an important defensive leader during the Sachems' improved season. The 34–0 Salem shutout and competitive defensive effort against Swampscott provide team context, but no individual tackles are assigned from those reports.
alumni.source: Contemporary contributed newspaper clippings and season history; official college and professional records where cited.

alumni.name: Mike Nicolo
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee (Class of 2026). A four-year starter and team captain his senior year, he set a then–single-game rushing record with 306 yards against Salem as a junior. He earned Lynn Item All-Scholastic honors that same season. He contributed as a freshman in 2001, rushing for 52 yards on eight carries at Beverly. As a sophomore, he ran for 76 yards at Swampscott and scored on a 52-yard run against Lynn English. He injured his right knee in the 2004 opener against Revere and remained a central part of the offense while battling injuries. In the surviving 11 game-scoring summaries he is credited with at least seven rushing touchdowns: 61 yards against Revere, four yards against Winthrop, six and two yards against Salem, 11 and one yards against Lynn English, and one yard against Swampscott. He also converted two-point runs against Lynn English and Swampscott. Surviving game reports document 429 rushing yards for Nicolo across six games. He ran for 54 yards on 21 carries at Winthrop, 67 yards on 16 carries against Salem, 73 yards on 19 carries against Beverly, 25 yards against Gloucester, 125 yards on 34 carries against Lynn English and 85 yards at Swampscott. In the Swampscott game, he also caught a 14-yard pass and ran for a two-point conversion before leaving in the fourth quarter with a knee injury. The Item also honored him in winter track as a sophomore, when he won the 300 meters in five dual meets, and in baseball as a junior, when he led Saugus with 30 hits and batted .390 as a second baseman.

His 2003 Item All-Star capsule credits him with 1,462 rushing yards on 260 carries and 11 touchdowns, NEC All-Star honors and Herald and Globe player-of-the-week recognition. The Lynn Item reported that he followed his record-setting Salem game with 241 rushing yards and all four Saugus touchdowns in a 29–14 win at Beverly. He rushed for 547 yards and scored seven touchdowns in the two wins. The Item’s weekly roundup credited him with 122 yards on 31 carries, a rushing touchdown and three catches in the double-overtime opener against Revere. The game box credits him with 39 receiving yards and a 50-yard completion to Kevin Davis. On Thanksgiving against Peabody, he rushed for 86 yards, threw a 28-yard touchdown pass to Kevin Davis and ran in the two-point conversion. His senior team finished 0–11 in 2004.

He continued his football career at Curry College, contributing at defensive back and on special teams during the Colonels’ championship era. Curry’s 12–1 team from the 2007 season, later inducted into the college’s Athletic Hall of Fame in 2021, won the NEFC title and defeated Hartwick 42–21 for the program’s first NCAA playoff victory. Nicolo recorded three tackles in the following playoff round at St. John Fisher. Curry later defeated his father John’s alma mater, Ithaca, 26–21 in the 2008 playoffs; a contemporary Ithaca preview reports that a shoulder injury had kept Mike out that season.

With his induction into the Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame in 2026, Mike joins his grandfather, Salvatore “Sardi” Nicolo, and his father, John Nicolo, in the Hall. Together, they become the first three generations of one family to be inducted into the school’s Athletic Hall of Fame—a milestone in the Nicolo family’s Saugus sports legacy. His brother Sal was a two-way starter for the Sachems at fullback and linebacker in 2001 and 2002.

Nicolo scored three touchdowns in the 34–0 Salem win, where his 306 rushing yards set the school record at the time. The 2003 Beverly game recap describes touchdown runs of 10, 10 and 5 yards; other surviving game accounts describe an additional scoring run, so the play-by-play and season total should be reconciled before replacing the published 11-touchdown season figure. The Thanksgiving preview described Nicolo as a pivotal runner behind an offensive line featuring Anthony Barbanti and Mark Spadafora.

alumni.name: Brett Reid
alumni.bio:
As a sophomore in 2006, Brett Reid quarterbacked a memorable Thanksgiving victory: he ran for 73 yards on 12 carries in the rain as Saugus shut out Peabody, 13–0, ending an 18-year wait for a win over the Tanners.

A three-year starting quarterback and two-time Lynn Item All-Scholastic, Brett Reid helped lead a resurgence in Sachems football. As a junior in 2007, he teamed with Tyler Trainor, Paul Sullivan and Mike Dean to guide Saugus to a 7–3 record—its first winning season since 1997.

Operating in a run-heavy offense, Reid rushed for 797 yards and 13 touchdowns that season. He and Dean helped Saugus repeat its 7–3 finish in 2008, with Reid contributing 800 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns.

His senior Item capsule also identifies Reid as a captain and a two-time Northeastern Conference All-Star. As a junior, he directed an option offense that the paper credited with averaging 23 points per game. The consecutive Item selections recognize his importance as both the offense’s decision-maker and a productive runner.

His college football career continued at UMass Dartmouth, whose rosters list him as a quarterback in 2009 and a wide receiver in 2010, under the spelling Bret Reid.
alumni.source: Contemporary contributed newspaper clippings and season history; official college and professional records where cited.

alumni.name: Justin Winn
alumni.bio:
Justin Winn earned Lynn Item All-Scholastic honors in both his junior and senior seasons. His 2013 junior Item capsule credits him with 1,103 rushing yards and 19 touchdowns, providing a standout individual performance during a difficult 3–8 season for the Sachems.

In 2014, Winn and running back Dan Cacciola helped lead Saugus to a 6–5 record. Winn rushed for 1,255 yards and set a school record with 22 rushing touchdowns.

His senior Item capsule also identifies him as a captain and Northeastern Conference All-Star and records a five-touchdown performance against Lynn English.
alumni.source: Contemporary contributed newspaper clippings and season history; official college and professional records where cited.

alumni.name: Braden Faiella
alumni.bio:
A two-time captain and two-time Lynn Item All-Star, Braden Faiella was the Item’s Defensive Player of the Year as a senior in 2023. His junior capsule reports 184 tackles; his senior profile records 140 tackles and a career total of 482. That final season also included an interception returned for a touchdown, five forced fumbles and four fumble recoveries. He contributed on the offensive line as well as at linebacker.

Saint Anselm’s biography also credits him with three first-team NEC selections, four years on the honor roll and participation in basketball, track and baseball at Saugus.

He continued his career at Saint Anselm College, whose 2026 roster lists him as a junior linebacker from Saugus. At Saint Anselm, he appeared against American International on October 18, 2025, recording two assisted tackles after not seeing game action in 2024.

alumni.name: Carlo Abate
alumni.bio:
Carlo Abate was a three-year starting linebacker and a defensive leader during Saugus’ rebuilding years of the mid-1990s. He earned Lynn Item All-Star and Northeastern Conference All-Star recognition in both 1994 and 1995, combining consistent tackling with an ability to create turnovers.

As a junior in 1994, Abate led his team and the area with more than 120 tackles. His Item capsule highlights 22 tackles against Lynn English, which earned him a Gold Helmet award, and another 19 stops against Lynn Classical. Those performances established him as one of the region’s most productive young linebackers.

As a senior in 1995, he overcame knee and shoulder injuries to lead the Sachems with 115 tackles, adding four interceptions and four fumble recoveries. His contribution was central to a season of renewal: Saugus ended its 34-game losing streak with a 25–0 victory over Winthrop and finished 6–4 for its first winning season since 1990. The report of the breakthrough win credits Abate with 14 tackles and identifies him and Dan Vass as pillars of the defense. His two Item capsules preserve both the individual production and the resilience behind that team turnaround.

The contributed Saugus season-history workbook also records Abate’s selection for the 1996 Agganis All-Star game, extending his recognition beyond his two Item and NEC All-Star seasons.

alumni.name: Edward “Eddie” Shipulski
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1988.

Edward “Eddie” Shipulski was a major backfield star during one of Saugus High's finest football eras. A three-season player, he helped the Sachems win the 1939 North Shore championship and the 1941 Class C state championship, finishing that fall unbeaten. The 1940 yearbook singled him out as a sophomore standout after he scored twice in a 26–0 victory over Gloucester. He also scored a touchdown in the 38–6 Thanksgiving win over Danvers that fall. By his senior season, Shipulski and John “Iron Mike” Harrington formed the backfield partnership the yearbook called its “touchdown twins.” Shipulski's 1941 highlights included touchdown runs of 70 yards against Gloucester, 57 yards against Amesbury, and 87 yards against Swampscott. A newspaper preview credited him with a team-leading 84 points entering Thanksgiving, despite an arm injury that limited his late-season action. He received Boston Globe All-Scholastic honorable mention and also played varsity baseball.

alumni.name: Michael “Mike” Garofano
alumni.bio: Michael Garofano helped lead Saugus High's return to organized football in 1914. A September newspaper feature identified him as captain and left halfback of a team being rebuilt after a lengthy interruption. By the time of a 1917 preseason report, Garofano was serving in France during World War I, and Saugus was preparing to select a replacement captain. His surviving clippings preserve both an early leader of the revived football program and a young Saugus serviceman whose life extended beyond the playing field.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Franklin “Oozo” Pike
alumni.bio:
Franklin “Oozo” Pike was a powerful, versatile fullback on Fred Beresford’s unbeaten 1922 Saugus team. Contemporary coverage praised his strength as a runner and his passing, kicking and drop-kicking, making him a triple threat in Beresford’s open offense. The Daily Evening Item reported that he had worked on his family’s East Saugus farm before playing high school football.

Pike had already produced game-changing plays in 1921. His 55-yard punt return supplied the only touchdown in a 6–0 victory over Methuen on November 11, and his 75-yard interception return for a touchdown helped beat Rockland 16–6 at Little River playground on November 25. The game had been postponed from Thanksgiving afternoon.

On October 12, 1922, Pike scored twice in a 14–7 win at Methuen, including a 65-yard first-quarter run. Nine days later he scored the only touchdown against Wellesley after captain Edward Amery’s 95-yard run set up the winning score. In the 1922 season finale, a 20–9 victory over Woburn, the Globe pictured Pike going over for a first-quarter touchdown and named Pike and captain Amery as Saugus’ standouts. Pike scored twice and also broke a 60-yard run before being tackled. That team finished 9–0–2 and is recorded in the archive as the Greater Lynn League champion.
alumni.source: Reviewed against contributed newspaper scans and yearbooks, existing honors records and applicable official college/professional sources, November 2026.

sources.label: Boston Globe · November 25, 1921 · Rockland postseason win

alumni.name: Edward Amery
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1992.

Captain Edward Amery supplied leadership and versatility to Saugus High's unbeaten 1922 eleven. The contemporary profile of the team praised him as a passer, receiver, interceptor, and its leading punter. Alongside Franklin Pike, Lester Pool, and quarterback Forest Kenerson, Amery helped give a relatively light squad the skill and adaptability to compete successfully under Fred Beresford. His captaincy and contributions in several roles helped shape one of Saugus's earliest outstanding teams.

His receiving produced a documented early highlight in the 16–6 postseason victory over Rockland on November 25, 1921: the Boston Globe credits Amery with catching a forward pass and running 32 yards for Saugus’ first touchdown.

In 1922, Amery added both extra points in the 14–7 win at Methuen. With about a minute left against Wellesley, his 95-yard run set up Franklin Pike’s touchdown in a 6–0 win. In the 20–9 season-ending victory over Woburn in 1922, he scored the opening touchdown, kicked two extra points and returned an interception to midfield.

alumni.name: John “Jack” Leahy
alumni.bio:
John Leahy was a captain and fullback during Albion Rice’s early years at Saugus. A newspaper feature identifies him as captain of the 1926 team and a junior fullback expected to return the following fall. It compared his summer work delivering heavy blocks of ice with the conditioning associated with football celebrity Red Grange. The later yearbook account places him among the experienced players around whom the successful 1927 team was built, preserving his importance as both a backfield player and a veteran leader. He was inducted into the Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame in 1992.

Leahy returned as head coach in 1935 and 1936. His first team won seven varsity games, according to the town report. The Sachems nickname dates to his tenure.

alumni.name: Reginald “Reggie” Goss
alumni.bio: Reggie Goss was an experienced leader of Saugus football in the late 1920s. He contributed at end to the 1927 team that won seven of eleven games, including a touchdown reception against Hyannis when Saugus turned to the pass to break through. He was then elected captain for 1928. The yearbook records his work at quarterback and end, his responsibility for the team's punting, and his determination despite an injury carried over from the previous season. In the muddy Thanksgiving game against Mission High, he caught Stuart Kidder's long pass and continued downfield on a play that gained more than sixty yards. The same yearbook records his election to the Scholastic Association with an 85 average, alongside teammate Gilman Cann.
alumni.source: Reviewed against contributed newspaper scans and yearbooks, existing honors records and applicable official college/professional sources, November 2026.

alumni.name: James “Jim” Foley
alumni.bio: Jim Foley earned a memorable place in the 1928 yearbook through his passing, tackling, and upbeat approach to football. Playing with one arm, he was praised for his judgment and effectiveness as well as his determination. The season account lists him among the quarterbacks and commends his backfield work against a heavier Mission High team on Thanksgiving. Foley's story offers a distinctive portrait of an early Saugus player whose teammates valued his ability, attitude, and willingness to take on the game's demands.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Stuart Kidder
alumni.bio: Stuart Kidder made a strong impression at fullback during the 1928 season. Although he had never played football before that fall, he won the fullback position and, according to the yearbook, gained more yardage than any other Saugus player. His most vividly recalled play came against Mission High on Thanksgiving, when he escaped pressure and threw a long pass to Reggie Goss for a gain exceeding sixty yards. The yearbook regarded his combination of running ability and promise as one of the bright spots of a demanding season.
alumni.source: Reviewed against contributed newspaper scans and yearbooks, existing honors records and applicable official college/professional sources, November 2026.

alumni.name: James “Jim” Muzzy
alumni.bio:
James Muzzy was a versatile halfback and captain of Saugus High's 1930 football team. When the lettermen elected him, Coach Albion Rice described him as the squad's best all-around player. The yearbook tribute credited Muzzy with consistent running, blocking, tackling, and passing, and ranked him behind only Laurie Templeman as a scoring threat. His leadership helped define a team remembered in the yearbook as Saugus's best since the unbeaten 1922 eleven.

He was already contributing to the scoring before his captaincy: the 1929 season account credits him with a touchdown in the 27–6 victory over Rockport, alongside Laurie Templeman’s three long scores.
alumni.source: Reviewed against contributed newspaper scans and yearbooks, existing honors records and applicable official college/professional sources, November 2026.

sources.label: 1929 season · Muzzy touchdown in the Rockport victory

alumni.name: Laurence “Laurie” Templeman
alumni.bio:
Laurence “Laurie” Templeman was one of Saugus High's outstanding running threats at the turn of the 1930s. In 1929, he scored both touchdowns in the 12–0 victory over Swampscott that the yearbook described as Saugus's first football win over that opponent. Against Swampscott, he scored on a short crossing play and a 25-yard cutback run. In the 27–6 victory over Rockport, his three touchdown runs covered 70, 44 and 35 yards. The same season review credits him with two touchdowns and two conversion kicks in the 22–0 opener over Manchester, demonstrating that he contributed with his foot as well as his running. The following season's tribute praised his speed, scoring, and ability to threaten opponents whenever he carried the ball. Together with captain Jim Muzzy, Templeman gave Coach Rice an accomplished backfield pairing.

The 1931 Tontoquonian lists Templeman in the senior class with four years each of football and baseball. He captained the baseball team as a senior and played left field.

At Northeastern, newspaper accounts called him Larry Templeman. He joined the freshman backfield in 1932 and earned varsity letters at halfback from 1933 through 1935. The 1935 preseason coverage identified him as one of four returning lettermen expected to start most games. A report after the season opener against American International described him as a standout halfback and noted that he aggravated an existing injury. He appears in the back row, third from the left, in the newspaper photo of Huskies who finished their careers against Massachusetts State. Northeastern won that finale 13–12 to finish unbeaten at 5–0–3.

alumni.name: Charles “Charlie” Murphy
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1999.

Charles “Charlie” Murphy, Class of 1952, was a standout two-way guard for three seasons and a member of Saugus’s 1949 and 1950 Exchange Bowl championship teams. He returned as a co-captain in 1951 and earned All-Scholastic selections from the Boston Globe, Boston Post, Lynn Item and R.A.A. The Globe named him to both its main All-Scholastic team and its Class A team, listing the senior at 5 feet 9 inches and 181 pounds.

The Globe’s 1951 profile describes Murphy repeatedly breaking into opposing backfields to disrupt T-formation handoffs, pressure passers and block kicks. He blocked four kicks that season and scored touchdowns on two of them. Coach John Janusas praised the many different methods Murphy used to penetrate an opposing line. An earlier Globe “Schoolboy Stars” feature also credited him with calling defensive signals and playing without missing a game over two seasons.

Charlie followed his brother Dan Murphy, another accomplished Saugus lineman. The 1951 Globe profile identifies Dan as a former Globe honoree then playing at the University of Connecticut. Charlie had not yet selected a college when the profile appeared.

One of those kick-blocking scores came in the 24–6 opening win over Revere in September 1951: Murphy blocked a punt and returned it for a touchdown. His statewide recognition also extended back to 1950, when the Globe listed him among its All-Scholastic honorable mentions at guard.

In 1950, Murphy recovered a fumble that set up a touchdown in the 39–0 win over Lynn English. The Exchange Bowl report singled out Murphy and co-captain Leo Kane for leading a line that held Brockton to 36 rushing yards.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Jim Driscoll
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2006.

Jim Driscoll was a Lynn Item All-Scholastic halfback on Saugus High's 1950 Exchange Bowl championship team. His versatility helped the Sachems early in the season, when he moved to quarterback while Richie Nicolo was unavailable. The Football Folio records his passing connection with Charlie Woodell and his later contributions as a runner. Driscoll helped give the 8–2 Sachems an adaptable backfield during the season that ended with a 30–12 Exchange Bowl victory over Brockton.

The Football Folio gives specific examples of his versatility: against Brookline, Driscoll threw two touchdown passes to Charlie Woodell, whose scoring plays covered 20 and 33 yards. Back at halfback against Lynn English, he scored on runs of 70, 40 and 35 yards in a 39–0 victory. He also scored in the 41–6 win over Salem. The Globe named him an All-Scholastic honorable mention at halfback in 1950, and the North Shore roster for the December 1950 North Shore–Suburban all-star game included him at right halfback.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Tony Serino
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2004.

Tony Serino contributed to the backfield during Saugus's successful transition from the Exchange Bowl years into the early 1950s. The 1950 Football Folio records two touchdown runs against Chelsea during the season that produced a second consecutive Exchange Bowl championship. In 1951, he shared the captaincy with Charlie Murphy and earned Lynn Item All-Scholastic recognition as a utility back. His scoring, leadership, and regional selection marked his contributions during these seasons.

He returned as Saugus’s quarterback in 1951, moving from fullback to direct the offense. In the 24–6 opening victory over Revere before approximately 4,000 spectators, Serino threw a 58-yard touchdown pass to Bob Meagher that put Saugus ahead 12–6. That passing play complemented the running and defensive scores in a win over a rival that had not beaten Saugus since 1920.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Robert “Bob” Belyea
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1999.

Bob Belyea was an honored lineman on Saugus High's 1953 North Shore League championship team. The 1954 yearbook records four years of football participation and identifies Belyea and Bill Whittredge as first-string selections on the Lynn All-Star team. The Boston Globe named Belyea to its Class A All-Star team at guard and listed him among its overall All-Scholastic reserves in December 1953. His individual recognition complemented his contributions to a championship team.

The championship yearbook singled out the line play of Belyea, Doug MacNeill and Bob Randazzo in the 21–0 league-opening victory over Lynn Classical, crediting them with stopping Classical’s drives. Saugus ultimately finished 6–1–1 and clinched its North Shore League title by beating Peabody 33–6 on Thanksgiving.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Bill Whittredge
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1996.

Bill Whittredge helped give Saugus its productive backfield during the 1953 North Shore League championship season. The 1954 yearbook records that he had been voted the best back of the previous year and names him, alongside Bob Belyea, as a first-string selection on the Lynn All-Star team during the class's championship senior year. The yearbook preserves his contributions to John Janusas's title-winning team.

Whittredge delivered several important scores during that championship run. His fourth-quarter touchdown run helped Saugus rally for a 12–12 tie with Marblehead. He scored Saugus’s first touchdown in the 14–13 win over Beverly and helped drive the late winning possession. He also scored in the 21–0 victory over Lynn Classical and 26–18 win over Lynn English. In the title-clinching 33–6 Thanksgiving win over Peabody, his runs repeatedly advanced the offense, and he threw a 50-yard pass to Dave Donaldson that put Saugus on the five-yard line during another scoring drive.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: John Leahy
alumni.bio:
John Leahy helped lead Saugus High to the 1953 North Shore League championship as a co-captain with Doug MacNeill. His senior biography records four years of football, and the class history identifies both captains as second-string selections on the Lynn All-Star team. The Sachems finished 6–1–1 in regular-season play and secured the title with a 33–6 Thanksgiving victory over Peabody. Leahy's captaincy and individual recognition preserve his place among the leaders of that championship team.

Leahy made a direct defensive contribution in the critical 14–13 victory over Beverly: the yearbook credits him, Bob Randazzo and Bob Krzywicki with catching a Beverly back behind the goal line for a safety. Those two points proved decisive in a one-point win. Against Salem, he recovered a fumble at the Salem 15-yard line; three plays later, Bob Piwowarski scored to complete the 27–0 victory.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Douglas “Doug” MacNeill
alumni.bio:
Doug MacNeill was a co-captain of Saugus High's 1953 North Shore League champions and a four-year football participant. The yearbook identifies him and fellow captain John Leahy as second-string Lynn All-Star selections. MacNeill also participated in basketball and baseball, reflecting the broad athletic involvement common to that generation of Sachems.

MacNeill helped set up Saugus’s opening touchdown in the 21–0 league win over Lynn Classical by recovering a fumble. The same account praised his line work, alongside Bob Belyea and Bob Randazzo, for stopping Classical’s drives. Those contributions helped the Sachems build the championship season that ended 6–1–1, capped by a 33–6 Thanksgiving victory over Peabody.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Bob Piwowarski
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2004.

Bob Piwowarski was a prominent runner on Saugus High's 6–3 team in 1954 and earned Lynn Item All-Scholastic recognition at back. The yearbook recalls his touchdown during the opening 20–0 win over Revere and his contribution to an offense that also featured Mal Rice, Fred Case, and Charlie Lawrence. His newspaper selection and repeated appearances in the season accounts place him among the notable Sachems of the middle 1950s.

Piwowarski had already contributed to the 1953 North Shore League champions as an underclassman. He scored the first touchdown in the 21–0 win over Lynn Classical. In the crucial 14–13 win over Beverly, his 21-yard run helped the first touchdown drive, and his scoring plunge finished Saugus’s late winning possession after Beverly had taken the lead in the closing minutes. He added the final touchdown in a 27–0 win over Salem. As a senior in 1954, he also scored in the 61–0 victory over Winthrop.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Richard “Dick” Rohrbacher
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2002.

Dick Rohrbacher was a captain and a recognized lineman for Saugus High in the late 1950s. The Item selected him at tackle on its 1957 North Shore All-Star team, listing him as a senior. The Boston Globe also named him an All-Scholastic honorable mention at tackle in its 1957 “On the Bench” selections; the clipping misspells his surname as Rhorbacker.

Rohrbacher was also selected for the North Shore squad in the December 1957 Harry Agganis Memorial All-Star game at Lynn’s Manning Bowl. The Globe’s pregame probable lineup listed him at right guard, showing his recognition extended beyond his usual tackle position.

alumni.name: John Dancewicz
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2000.

John Dancewicz was a co-captain of Saugus High's 7–2 football team in 1966 and a first-team Lynn Item All-Star. The Item honored his line play at tackle, while the yearbook also identifies him as a back. Dancewicz also served as senior class president and appears among the year's National Merit finalists, giving his profile a documented combination of football leadership and academic accomplishment.

A 1967 newspaper profile identifies his two-way roles more specifically as offensive tackle and defensive linebacker. Following the 1966 season, Dancewicz became the first New England student to receive the national $1,000 scholarship associated with the Thom McAn football trophy. Selected from players representing more than 850 teams, he was recognized for sportsmanship, scholarship, teamwork, leadership and competitive spirit, together with his essay on attending college. He ranked third in his class of 350 and was the nephew of Notre Dame All-American Boley Dancewicz. The Globe also listed him among its 1966 All-Scholastic honorable mentions at tackle.

alumni.name: James “Jim” Mancuso
alumni.bio:
Jim Mancuso was a first-team Lynn Item All-Star tackle on Saugus High's successful 1966 team. The newspaper listed him at 6-foot-1 and 205 pounds, and the yearbook preserves his individual football portrait. His senior biography records four years of football and hockey and identifies him as a hockey co-captain. Mancuso combined individual football recognition with participation across several sports.

Mancuso earned a further regional distinction when the Globe’s August 18, 1967 Agganis preview listed him as a projected starting guard for the North squad at Manning Bowl. The article identified the University of Connecticut as his intended college.

alumni.name: Edward “Eddie” Maguire
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1988.

Edward Maguire was a backfield leader and co-captain of Saugus High's 7–2 team in 1966. He earned first-team Lynn Item All-Star recognition at back, joining teammates John Dancewicz and Jim Mancuso on the selected team. The yearbook preserves his co-captain portrait alongside Dancewicz and Paul Uga, documenting the leadership group behind one of Saugus's strongest seasons of the decade.

He ran for 150 yards and two touchdowns in a 33–6 season-opening win over B.C. High. He also scored against Marblehead after Jim Paolini’s interception set up the drive in a 29–0 shutout.

The Globe named Maguire an All-Scholastic honorable mention at back in 1966, and its August 18, 1967 Agganis preview listed him as a projected North starting halfback, with Indiana as his intended college.

At Indiana University, he moved to defensive end and earned football letters in 1969 and 1970. Indiana’s official record book credits him with 17 tackles for loss in each season, for a career total of 34, and lists him as a second-team All-Big Ten selection in 1970. These college achievements add a major-conference defensive career to his Saugus backfield accomplishments.

alumni.name: James “Jim” Fauci
alumni.bio: James Fauci captained Saugus High during Buzz Harvey's first season as head coach in 1937. His senior yearbook praised his alert, determined play and the example he set for his teammates. The team opened with five consecutive victories over Marblehead, Barnstable, Gloucester, Amesbury and Woburn and finished 7–2–1. Its yearbook celebrated the opening win over traditional rival Marblehead and the strong start under Harvey; the Thanksgiving finale against Danvers ended in a 6–6 tie. His yearbook tribute preserves an important leadership figure from the late 1930s.

alumni.name: Earl Hanson
alumni.bio: Earl Hanson was a three-season football participant and captain of Saugus High's 1938 team. His senior yearbook remembered a quiet leader whose courage helped set the tone for his teammates. The Sachems finished 6–4 and closed with a 6–0 Thanksgiving victory over Danvers. Hanson's captaincy links the early years of Buzz Harvey's program with the greater success that followed in 1939.

alumni.name: Michael “Mike” Light
alumni.bio:
Michael Light was a co-captain of Saugus High's 1958 football team and earned second-team Lynn Item North Shore All-Star recognition at end. His senior biography records three seasons of football and four years of hockey, preserving the range of his athletic participation. Light shared the football captaincy with John Naples.

He was also named in the lineup of the Lynn–Swampscott All-Stars for their 14–6 victory over Salem–Beverly in the third annual Harry Agganis Memorial game at Manning Bowl on December 7, 1958. The Globe’s game report listed Light among the winning side’s ends.

alumni.name: David Russell “Dave” Mathews
alumni.bio:
David Russell “Dave” Mathews, Saugus High Class of 1960, was a football co-captain and quarterback on the Sachems’ recognized 1959 championship team. The Lynn Item named him a first-team North Shore football All-Star at back in 1959. A four-year participant in football, he was among the final graduating players to compete under longtime Saugus coach John Janusas. His senior yearbook and the team’s portrait collection preserve his leadership and broad athletic ability.

Mathews helped deliver a memorable 14–6 Thanksgiving victory over Peabody in 1959 before approximately 8,500 fans at Stackpole Field. He threw the first-period touchdown pass to end Frank Bucchiere and ran for the two-point conversion, giving Saugus an 8–0 lead. The victory spoiled Peabody’s Class A title opportunity. The Globe also listed D. R. Mathews among its 1959 All-Scholastic honorable mentions at back.

Mathews also excelled in hockey and baseball. A hockey co-captain and four-year participant in both sports, he earned Essex County League hockey All-Star recognition three times and was Saugus’s leading hockey scorer, according to The Saugus Advocate’s retrospective. The Saugus High School Alumni Association’s July 2011 newsletter identifies him in the photograph of the 1959–60 championship hockey team.

His athletic career continued beyond Saugus: The Saugus Advocate reports that he was heavily recruited and went on to play hockey at Boston College. His college seasons, statistics and honors have not yet been established by the sources reviewed.

Mathews was inducted into the Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame in 1989. The Advocate later included him among its “Terrific Twenty-Five” Saugus Hall of Famers, recognizing his achievements across football, hockey and baseball.

alumni.name: Richard “Richie” Burt
alumni.bio:
Richard Burt was a fullback on Saugus High's recognized 1959 championship team and earned second-team Lynn Item North Shore All-Star recognition. His senior biography records four years each of football and baseball and specifically praises his running for the champion football team. The yearbook's award list also names him as recipient of the John A. W. Pearce Football Award. Burt combined team success with regional recognition and a school football award.

Burt scored the winning touchdown in the 1959 Thanksgiving upset of Peabody. After Saugus stopped a fourth-down pass at the Peabody 20 in the fourth quarter, the Sachems drove for the decisive score, with Burt carrying over from the one-yard line. The 14–6 victory, watched by approximately 8,500 fans, denied Peabody a chance at the Class A title.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

His senior biography also records track, volleyball and gymnastics participation, while the football section preserves his captaincy and role in the team's late-season improvement.
