alumni.name: Robert “Bob” Osgood
alumni.bio:
At Saugus, Osgood earned first-team Lynn Item All-Star recognition at back and first-team Northeastern Conference offensive honors in 1969. He completed 54 passes for 1,157 yards and eight touchdowns and earned Boston Globe Class B All-Star and All-Scholastic bench recognition. In a 30–6 win over Winthrop, he threw a 99-yard touchdown to John Richard. Against Watertown, he passed for a touchdown and two conversions to Greg Manship and ran for another score. He quarterbacked a 7–2 team whose only losses came against Class A champion Peabody and Class B champion Swampscott. He was then selected as one of the North squad’s quarterbacks for the 1970 Harry Agganis All-Star game. A Globe pregame feature described him as a drop-back passer being coached to add roll-out plays against the South’s heavier defensive line.

Bob Osgood, Saugus High Class of 1970, quarterbacked the Sachems before continuing his football career at the University of New Hampshire. The Saugus Advocate’s retrospective describes him as heavily recruited and identifies him as a starting quarterback at UNH. The university’s own archives confirm his membership on the 1973 football team under head coach Bill Bowes, identifying him by name in the team photograph. His complete college football seasons, individual statistics and starting assignments remain to be established from contemporary records.

Osgood was also an accomplished basketball and baseball player at Saugus. He played three years of high-school basketball and was a right-handed pitcher on Saugus’s 1970 state-tournament baseball team. His two-sport college career is supported by UNH’s archives, which identify him in both the 1971 and 1972 baseball team photographs. The Advocate remembers him as an outstanding pitcher at UNH as well as a college quarterback.

He was inducted into the Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame in 1990. The Saugus Advocate later included him among its “Terrific Twenty-Five” Saugus Hall of Famers.

alumni.name: Raphael Zammit
alumni.source: Newspaper clippings and college records. Contributed 1997 newspaper scoring summaries.
alumni.bio:
As a junior in 1997, Zammit scored on a 75-yard kickoff return against Danvers and a 65-yard catch against Swampscott. The available scoring summaries document nine touchdowns that fall, including five catches, three runs and the kickoff return.

Senior captain Raphael Zammit earned Boston Globe All-Scholastic honors at tailback and strong safety in 1998, along with Lynn Item and Northeastern Conference All-Star honors. He rushed for 1,481 yards and 21 rushing touchdowns, a school record at the time. He scored 25 total touchdowns and led Division 3 with 154 points. The Item reports 2,452 all-purpose yards and the Globe reports 2,453. On defense, he had 52 tackles, eight sacks and three interceptions, returning one for a touchdown. The Globe credited him with 2,891 rushing yards, 4,653 all-purpose yards and 41 touchdowns over his Saugus career. He was named South MVP in the 1999 Agganis All-Star game.

At Curry College from 2000 through 2003, Zammit rushed for 4,353 career yards and 44 touchdowns. He earned second-team all-conference honors in 2000 and 2001, then first-team honors and conference Offensive Player of the Year in 2002 and 2003. As a junior in 2002, he was named a third-team running back on the Hewlett Packard Division III All-America team. Curry’s records also list third-team All-America honors in 2003. He rushed for 1,479 yards in 2002 and 1,587 in 2003.

alumni.name: Marvens Jean
alumni.bio:
Marvens Jean earned Lynn Item All-Star recognition as a senior in 2019, contributing as both a runner and defensive back. His senior profile records 1,074 rushing yards, 12 rushing touchdowns, 87 tackles, two forced fumbles and a kickoff return for a touchdown.

At UMass Dartmouth, his roster career spanned 2020–2024 and included both running back and wide receiver. He earned second-team All-MASCAC honors in 2021 after rushing for 772 yards and five touchdowns, then ran for 254 yards against Husson in 2022. Moving to wide receiver in 2023, he caught 42 passes for 544 yards. Back at running back in 2024, he rushed for 540 yards over the season and contributed 79 yards and a touchdown in the MASCAC title-clinching victory over Plymouth State.

alumni.name: Dan Cacciola
alumni.bio:
Dan Cacciola set Saugus’s single-game rushing record with 375 yards and four touchdowns against Winthrop in 2014, as documented in the preserved Winthrop Transcript account.

His senior season produced 1,467 rushing yards and 18 rushing touchdowns in the Item’s season profile. He earned Lynn Item and Northeastern Conference All-Star honors, together with Boston Globe Eastern Massachusetts Division 4 All-Star recognition. Alongside fellow runner Justin Winn, Cacciola helped Saugus finish 6–5 in 2014. His school record and recognition from several selectors make him a standout of that era.

alumni.name: George Lowe
alumni.bio:
George Lowe was a captain and Lynn Item and Northeastern Conference All-Star during Saugus’s 1999 season. His senior Item profile credits him with 604 rushing yards, 27 catches for 148 yards, 72 tackles, four interceptions and two fumble recoveries. He scored nine touchdowns, including three in a 30–14 win over Marblehead and one on an 85-yard kickoff return against Salem. As a younger player in 1997, Lowe threw a 20-yard touchdown pass to Mike Panzini in a win over Lynn Classical.

He continued at Curry College as a cornerback. In 2003, he earned first-team all-conference and second-team ECAC All-Region honors. Curry’s record book credits him with 13 passes broken up that season, tied for second on the school’s season leaderboard when the book was updated in January 2025.

alumni.name: Paul Nigro
alumni.bio:
Paul Nigro was a senior captain and Lynn Item All-Star in 1978. His senior capsule credits him with 1,395 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns, complemented by 25 receptions for 360 yards and 14 kickoff returns for 207 yards.

Nigro’s combination of running, receiving and return work gave Saugus a versatile offensive threat. His preserved Item profile documents one of the program’s notable individual rushing seasons of the late 1970s.

Nigro also starred for Saugus High in ice hockey as a forward. In 1977–78, he recorded 21 goals and 21 assists for 42 points, leading the Northeastern Conference in scoring according to the Massachusetts high school tournament program. In 1978–79, he added 15 goals and 24 assists for 39 points. His documented two-season totals were 36 goals, 45 assists and 81 points. Elite Prospects lists him atop its Saugus High all-time recorded points table. College football or hockey participation has not been verified and is not included here.

The Boston Globe documented several of Nigro’s standout performances. In the 25–0 upset of favored Winthrop, the 5-foot-11, 192-pound senior rushed for 152 yards on 16 carries and scored three touchdowns, including an 87-yard opening kickoff return. Against Lynn English, he rushed for 271 yards on just eight carries in the first quarter, scoring on two long runs and an 83-yard touchdown reception for 354 total offensive yards; he had reached 13 season touchdowns at that point. In the Thanksgiving finale, he rushed for 165 yards and scored three touchdowns, including a 66-yard run, to lead a 30–14 win over Peabody. The Globe described him as one of Eastern Massachusetts’ top halfbacks.

Listed at 6-foot-1 and 205 pounds, he played tackle on both sides of the ball before shifting to offensive guard, and also saw action at defensive end. His Item profile credits him with 14 quarterback sacks and reports that his coaches rated him highest on the squad in all but one game. His pass rush and versatility made him a standout on the Sachems’ line.

alumni.name: Steve Spinney
alumni.bio:
Steve Spinney captained the 1974 Sachems and earned Lynn Item and Northeastern Conference All-Star recognition. The Item selected the 6-foot-2, 215-pound senior at offensive end and highlighted his versatility, noting that he played many positions. He helped lead Saugus to a 6–4 season under Mike Ginolfi. He returned an interception 39 yards for the deciding touchdown in the 12–7 win at Marblehead and caught a two-point pass in the win over Lynn Classical.

Steve is the son of fellow Saugus football great Art Spinney, Class of 1945, who captained Boston College and became an All-Pro lineman and two-time NFL champion with the Baltimore Colts. The contemporary Item profile explicitly identifies their father–son relationship, connecting two generations of Sachems football.

Colt Meredith’s football career culminated in national recognition at Plymouth State. The contributed 1993 Saugus preview identifies him as a senior, establishing his Saugus graduation class as 1994.

He played linebacker and defensive back for Plymouth State from 1996 through 1999 and captained the team in 1999. That fall, he was named Freedom Football Conference Defensive Player of the Year and earned Hewlett-Packard/SID Division III All-America honorable mention as a defensive back. His conference award, college captaincy and national recognition distinguish his career beyond Saugus.

alumni.name: Ryan Leahy
alumni.bio:
Ryan Leahy quarterbacked the Sachems from 1996 through 1998 and co-captained the 1998 team. As a sophomore in 1996, Leahy threw at least seven touchdown passes, including an 89-yarder to L.J. McKanas against Salem. As a junior in 1997, he completed 65 of 124 passes for 1,109 yards and 14 touchdowns and ran 35 times for 294 yards and four more scores. He accounted for four touchdowns in a 31–8 win over Danvers and threw the fourth-quarter winner to Chris McBride in a 24–20 victory at Salem. He helped Saugus finish 6–4–1 and earned Daily Evening Item and Northeastern Conference All-Star honors at quarterback.

Leahy earned a second NEC All-Star selection in 1998. Entering the Thanksgiving finale against Peabody, he had completed 43 of 82 passes for 825 yards and seven touchdowns, rushed for five touchdowns and also played free safety. He threw for two more touchdowns in the finale, bringing his documented senior totals to at least 880 passing yards and nine touchdown passes. The Boston Globe later credited him with 30 career touchdown passes, tying him for 25th on its historical Massachusetts list. Saugus newspaper records credit Steve Peach with 33 career touchdown passes across his three varsity seasons.

After Saugus, Leahy was listed as a wide receiver for Bentley College football in a contemporary newspaper clipping.

alumni.name: Kyle Sucharewicz
alumni.bio:
Kyle Sucharewicz quarterbacked the Sachems at the turn of the millennium. As a sophomore in 1999, he scored on a 14-yard run in the fourth quarter to beat Methuen 6–0. He threw touchdown passes of 65 yards to George Lowe and 10 yards to Mike Navarro in a 20–12 win over Swampscott. That fall, he earned Northeastern Conference and Eastern Massachusetts Division 3 All-Star honors at quarterback.

In 2000, Sucharewicz threw three touchdown passes in a 26–6 win at Marblehead, finding Mark Pizzotti, Patrick Eaton and Tom Shidlow. He also threw to Adam Magnasco for a two-point conversion. As a senior in 2001, he threw three touchdown passes as Saugus rallied from a 14–0 deficit to beat Salem 30–14.

Sucharewicz scored 1,180 career points for Saugus basketball from 1998 to 2002. The Saugus Advocate’s February 2026 scoring list ranked him second among Saugus boys, behind Alex Winn, and third on the combined boys’ and girls’ list. He returned to Saugus as a basketball coach. A 2014 profile reported that he had spent the previous five years as a varsity assistant and head junior varsity coach. He entered the Saugus High School Sports Hall of Fame in 2014 for football and basketball.

alumni.name: George Nicolo
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1996.

George Nicolo quarterbacked the Sachems during their 1977 Northeastern Conference championship season under head coach Mike Ginolfi. Saugus finished 9–1 and won the conference championship. Nicolo’s senior season stands as the school’s single-season passing-touchdown record: 15 touchdown passes. Contemporary season statistics credit him with 1,052 passing yards on 81 completions in 157 attempts, plus four successful conversion passes. He also scored two rushing touchdowns. The 15 passing touchdowns led Massachusetts Division II according to the contemporary season leaders chart.

His 1977 performances earned Lynn Item All-Star recognition at quarterback and selection to the Northeastern Conference offensive All-Star team. Nicolo was among the key players on one of the Sachems’ most successful teams of the 1970s. Saugus High School inducted him into its Athletic Hall of Fame in 1996.

alumni.name: John “Sal” Nicolo
alumni.bio:
John “Sal” Nicolo played football for Saugus High from 1999 through 2002 and graduated in 2003. He earned Freshman of the Year as the freshman team MVP in 1999. He wore his father John’s No. 1 his first two seasons and his grandfather Salvatore “Sardi” Nicolo’s No. 33 as a junior and senior. He started at fullback and linebacker in 2001 and 2002 under his father, the Sachems’ head coach.

As a junior, Nicolo scored on a five-yard run against Danvers. On Thanksgiving, he intercepted Peabody quarterback Mike Shah and returned it 33 yards for a touchdown. He also recovered a fumble in that game and earned a Lynn Item Top Performers mention. As a senior, he intercepted a pass in the opener at Belmont, rushed for more than 50 yards and scored from two yards out at Danvers, and ran for a touchdown against Gloucester. His 35-yard fumble return deep into Marblehead territory helped spark a 31–16 Saugus win. The Agganis Foundation selected him for the 2003 Harry Agganis All-Star Football Classic. He wore No. 31 for the South in its 24–14 win at Manning Bowl.

Nicolo joined the varsity wrestling program as a sophomore in 2000–01, won a match at 140 pounds in an early quad meet, and earned the team’s Rookie of the Year award. He went on to record pins against Somerville, Watertown and Minuteman and won a 152-pound decision at the Whittier Tech Tournament. He also competed in track for Saugus.

After graduation, he played linebacker at Bridgewater State College under Peter Mazzaferro in 2003 and 2004. Bridgewater’s records list him as John Nicolo (No. 38) in 2003, when he appeared in two games and recorded one solo tackle, and as Sal Nicolo (No. 55) in 2004, when he appeared in one game.
alumni.source: Sal’s Scrapbook and contributed game and wrestling clippings, the Nicolo family history and researcher profile, Agganis selection coverage, and Bridgewater State participation records. Freshman team MVP confirmed by Sal Nicolo.

alumni.name: Rodney Lavoie
alumni.bio: The 2006 captain led Saugus to a 13–0 Thanksgiving win over Peabody, its first victory over the Tanners in 18 years. The Boston Globe credited him with 186 yards on 35 carries. The Sachems won their final three games after an 0–7 start. His Lynn Item All-Star profile also highlighted a three-touchdown game against Holbrook. He earned Lynn Item and Northeastern Conference All-Star honors as a senior. In 2015, Lavoie finished fourth on CBS’s Survivor: Worlds Apart.
alumni.source: Boston Globe game report, Lynn Item All-Star profile, MaxPreps roster and Saugus season archive.

alumni.name: Tyler Trainor
alumni.bio: The 2007 captain anchored the defense on Saugus’s first winning team since 1997. He made 108 tackles, recovered seven fumbles and intercepted two passes, returning one for a touchdown. He also ran for five touchdowns as the Sachems finished 7–3. Trainor earned Lynn Item and Northeastern Conference All-Star honors, the Walter Boverini Defensive Player of the Year award and the Saugus Lions Club Heisman Trophy. He went on to play linebacker and safety at Bridgewater State from 2008 through 2011. Plymouth State’s box scores document his game appearances in 2010 and 2011.

alumni.name: Mike Dean
alumni.bio: Dean helped power consecutive 7–3 seasons under coach Mike Broderick and shared the captaincy with Bret Reid in 2008. The Lynn Item credited Dean with 1,242 rushing yards on 130 carries and 17 touchdowns as a senior. Its profile also reported two interception returns for touchdowns. He earned NEC recognition in 2007 and returned as an NEC Small All-Star in 2008, when he also earned Lynn Item and Eastern Massachusetts Division 3 All-Star honors. Dean played defensive back at UMass Dartmouth in 2009 and 2010. He started at free safety against Curry as a freshman.
alumni.source: Lynn Item profile, supplied All-Star lists, MaxPreps varsity statistics and UMass Dartmouth roster.

alumni.name: Tommy Trainor
alumni.bio: Trainor captained the 2012 Sachems and anchored the defense at middle linebacker. The Lynn Item credited him with 110 tackles, including seven for loss, as Saugus improved to 6–5 and shut out Peabody 43–0 on Thanksgiving. He earned Lynn Item and CAL/NEC All-Star honors and received the Saugus Heisman Trophy at the pre-Thanksgiving dinner. The Boston Globe profiled three generations of his football family. His father Tom and uncle Don, both former Sachems linebackers, were on the Saugus coaching staff. Bridgewater State listed Tommy as a freshman linebacker in 2013.
alumni.source: Lynn Item All-Star profile, Boston Globe family feature, Saugus Advocate graduation report and Bridgewater State roster.

alumni.name: Tommy DeSimone
alumni.bio: A captain on the 2023 team, DeSimone rushed for 1,113 yards and 14 touchdowns as Saugus opened 3–0 and finished 5–6. He ran 28 times for 140 yards and three touchdowns in a 28–22 win over Northeast, earning a Boston Globe Player of the Week mention. He also scored Saugus’s touchdown on a 13-yard run against Peabody on Thanksgiving. DeSimone earned Lynn Item honors at running back and was named Northeastern Conference Offensive All-Conference. In 2026, he played linebacker for Worcester State and recorded five tackles and two sacks against Dean College.
alumni.source: Saugus Advocate season profile and conference awards, Boston Globe weekly honors, Lynn Item honors archive and MaxPreps roster.

sources.label: Boston Globe · Week 2 Players of the Week
Dean College · Worcester State box score

alumni.name: Patrick “Pat” Eaton
alumni.bio: Eaton captained the 2001 Sachems and contributed as a runner, receiver and defensive back. His senior Lynn Item profile credits him with 545 rushing yards and 30 catches for 505 yards, for 1,050 yards from scrimmage. The game accounts include a 48-yard touchdown catch against Lynn Classical and a 19-yard touchdown run against Marblehead. Eaton earned Lynn Item and Northeastern Conference football All-Star honors, and the season archive records his selection for the 2002 Harry Agganis All-Star Football Classic.
alumni.source: Lynn Item senior profile, season box scores and Agganis archive.

alumni.name: Pat Quinlan
alumni.bio:
Quinlan started for four years on defense at Saugus and was a senior captain, according to the Boston Globe. He contributed on offense as well. In 2000, he scored both Saugus touchdowns in a 13–10 win at Swampscott, including the go-ahead 60-yard run. The archive lists him as a 2002 Harry Agganis football All-Star. His grandfather Fred was a Saugus running back and catcher, and his father, also named Fred, played on the line at Saugus and Plymouth State.

Quinlan played at Plymouth State from 2002 through 2005, moving from linebacker to the defensive line and captaining the Panthers as a senior. In 2004, he received the Fred Madore Award and the Jason D. Holder Award as Homecoming MVP. The Globe reported 35 tackles, seven for loss, in his senior season. His two blocked extra points helped preserve a 21–19 win over Husson and earned him a spot on the D3football.com Team of the Week.
alumni.source: Boston Globe feature, Saugus season archive and Plymouth State football records.

sources.label: Boston Globe · Patrick Quinlan and his football family

alumni.name: Fred Quinlan
alumni.bio:
Quinlan broke a 66-yard touchdown run in a 14–6 win over Marblehead in 1947 and went on to become one of the leading scorers on John Janusas’s 1949 team. He scored 10 regular-season touchdowns for 60 points as Saugus shared North Shore honors with Gloucester. The Sachems finished 10–1 after beating Weymouth 7–6 in the Exchange Bowl. Quinlan earned Lynn Item All-Scholastic recognition as a utility player and Boston Globe All-Scholastic honorable mention as a back.

Quinlan also caught for the Saugus baseball team. The Boston Globe identifies him as the grandfather of fellow Sachem football alumnus Pat Quinlan, Class of 2002. Saugus High inducted Fred into its Athletic Hall of Fame in 1995.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings, the Saugus season archive, Boston Globe family feature and school Hall of Fame list.

sources.label: Saugus High · 1995 Hall of Fame class

alumni.name: Pat Sullivan
alumni.bio: Sullivan helped anchor the right side of the offensive line alongside Doug Mackie on Mike Ginolfi’s 1975 Sachems. The Lynn Item highlighted his blocking at guard and his play at linebacker. Saugus went 9–1, posted six shutouts and shared the Northeastern Conference title with Salem. Sullivan was named a Lynn Item All-Star and earned NEC offensive All-Star honors on the interior line as a junior. He returned the next fall and captained the 1976 Sachems alongside Mark Calhoun. Saugus High inducted him into its Athletic Hall of Fame in 2003.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings, the Saugus season archive and the school’s Athletic Hall of Fame roster.

sources.label: 1975 NEC offensive and defensive All-Star roster
Saugus High · Athletic Hall of Fame roster

alumni.name: Tom Heaney
alumni.bio: Heaney contributed to Saugus’s 6–4 team in 1974, catching a touchdown pass from Mike Burt in a 26–14 win at Danvers. A year later, he co-captained the 9–1 Northeastern Conference co-champions with Doug Mackie, John Nicolo and Steve Gannon. The 1975 game summaries document six rushing touchdowns for Heaney. He ran for two scores in the 42–16 win over Lynn English and scored Saugus’s lone touchdown on a 30-yard run against Swampscott. He also caught a two-point pass from Jay LeBranti in the 15–14 comeback at Salem. Saugus High inducted Heaney into its Athletic Hall of Fame in 1993.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings, the Saugus season archive and the school’s Athletic Hall of Fame roster.

sources.label: Saugus High · Athletic Hall of Fame roster

alumni.name: Richard “Richie” Salerno
alumni.bio:
Richie Salerno played three seasons of football at Saugus High and was a senior on John Janusas’s 1953 North Shore League championship team. The yearbook noted his strong start that fall and his return from an injury suffered against Chelsea. He was back in the lineup for the 33–6 Thanksgiving win over Peabody that clinched the title and capped a 6–1–1 season.

After his playing days, Salerno returned to Sachem football as a coach. By 1971 he was teaching and coaching at Saugus High, working with students in the classroom and on the football field. He became a well-known and respected educator in Saugus and remained a familiar figure to people around the football program. Saugus High inducted him into its Athletic Hall of Fame in 2004.
alumni.source: 1954 Tontoquonian, Saugus High Athletic Hall of Fame roster, contemporary records of his teaching and coaching role, and archive contributor recollections.
